title: Functions, Structs, Enums, and Traits
summary: Design domain models with typed functions, structs, impl blocks, enums, traits, generics, visibility, and invariant-preserving constructors.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Functions, Structs, Enums, and Traits
Use compiler, lint, and test evidence to verify behavior
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Functions declare parameter and return types. Structs model related data, enums model a value that is exactly one of several variants, and methods live in `impl` blocks. Keep fields private when arbitrary mutation could violate invariants. A constructor conventionally named `new` can return `Result<Self, Error>` when validation may fail. Traits define shared behavior and are implemented explicitly. Generic bounds state required capabilities. Prefer enums over boolean combinations for meaningful states, because exhaustive matching keeps transitions visible.
keyPoints: Functions declare parameter and return types.
commonMistakes: shared and active mutable borrowing cannot overlap
only one active mutable borrow to the same data is allowed
